Markdown pads a code block with Padding and strips it in one pass (rich-unfiled-791c.ct7i review)

The trailing-whitespace regex was quadratic in an interior run; pyRstrip
scans from the end over the one PY_WHITESPACE set. The hand-built margin
is Padding, so at widths under three the code keeps a column before the
padding does, as every Padding does. The width is parsed once at the top
of Markdown.render.

Markdown draws a code block inside Syntax's margin, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.ct7i)

Rich's CodeBlock hands the code, rstripped, to Syntax(word_wrap=True,
padding=1). The block now draws through our Syntax the same way: word-wrapped
at width-2, tab stops of 4 (was 8), and a one-cell margin of the code's style
on every side. Trailing whitespace is Python's str.isspace set, not JS's \s.
Pinned against Rich 15 rows, including widths 1 and 2 where Rich draws only
the margin.

Markdown draws a rule in -, as Rich's HorizontalRule does (rich-unfiled-791c.x0d0) (#438)

* Markdown draws a rule in -, as Rich's HorizontalRule does (rich-unfiled-791c.x0d0)

* The quote-rule test quotes Rich's 36 dashes and names the tickets that own its divergences (rich-unfiled-791c.x0d0)
